---
title: "An interactive NGS sequencing-QC dashboard in JavaScript with CanvasXpress"
description: "Triage a 96-sample sequencing run in the browser: an overview QC heatmap plus linked, cross-filtering panels that flag failing samples and batch effects — from portable specs, no framework."
author: "Isaac Neuhaus"
date: "2026-10-31"
categories: [JavaScript, CanvasXpress, dashboard, bioinformatics, visualization]
image: "thumbnail.png"
---

After a sequencing run you get a QC table — one row per sample, a dozen metrics — and you need to
answer three questions fast: **which samples fail, is a whole batch off, and are the failures
correlated?** A single scatter can't do it; you want several views that **talk to each other** —
select a suspicious sample in one and see it light up in the rest. In the browser that usually means
wiring event handlers between chart libraries by hand. CanvasXpress does it for you: give every panel
the same **broadcast group** and a selection broadcasts to all of them. Here we build a real QC
dashboard for 96 RNA/exome samples.

## Load the library and the data

The 96-sample QC table is published next to this post as a small JS object,
[`qc-data.js`](qc-data.js) — `QC_DATA` is a sample-centric CanvasXpress `data` object (each sample is
a point; `z` holds its lane/batch/library).

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
<script src="qc-data.js"></script>
```

## The panels

The overview heatmap transposes the data to metrics × samples and z-scores each metric. The four
triage panels read `QC_DATA` directly and all share `broadcastGroup: "qc"` — select points in one and
the same samples re-mark in the rest.

```html
<canvas id="qcHeat" width="820" height="420"></canvas>
<canvas id="qcMap" width="640" height="360"></canvas>
<canvas id="qcContam" width="640" height="360"></canvas>
<canvas id="qcQ30" width="640" height="360"></canvas>
<canvas id="qcReads" width="820" height="300"></canvas>
<script>
  var metrics = QC_DATA.y.smps, samples = QC_DATA.y.vars, rows = QC_DATA.y.data;

  // Overview: transpose to metrics x samples and z-score each metric.
  var hmData = metrics.map(function (_, c) {
    var col = rows.map(function (r) { return r[c]; });
    var mean = col.reduce(function (a, b) { return a + b; }, 0) / col.length;
    var sd = Math.sqrt(col.reduce(function (a, b) { return a + (b - mean) * (b - mean); }, 0) / col.length) || 1;
    return col.map(function (v) { return Math.round((v - mean) / sd * 100) / 100; });
  });
  new CanvasXpress("qcHeat",
    { y: { vars: metrics, smps: samples, data: hmData },
      x: { Batch: QC_DATA.z.Batch, Library: QC_DATA.z.Library } },
    { graphType: "Heatmap", samplesClustered: true, variablesClustered: true,
      colorSpectrum: ["navy", "white", "firebrick3"],
      title: "QC metrics (z-scored) — 96 samples clustered" });

  // Linked triage panels (same QC_DATA, shared broadcast group).
  function panel(id, cfg) {
    new CanvasXpress(id, QC_DATA, Object.assign({ broadcast: true, broadcastGroup: "qc" }, cfg));
  }
  panel("qcMap", { graphType: "Scatter2D", xAxis: ["pct_duplication"], yAxis: ["pct_mapped"],
    colorBy: "Batch", sizeBy: "total_reads", title: "Mapping rate vs duplication — select bottom-right" });
  panel("qcContam", { graphType: "Scatter2D", xAxis: ["pct_mapped"], yAxis: ["contamination_freemix"],
    colorBy: "Batch", title: "Contamination (freemix) vs mapping rate" });
  panel("qcQ30", { graphType: "Scatter2D", xAxis: ["gc_content"], yAxis: ["pct_q30"],
    colorBy: "Library", title: "Q30 vs GC content, coloured by library" });
  panel("qcReads", { graphType: "Bar", graphOrientation: "vertical", xAxis: ["total_reads"],
    colorBy: "Batch", title: "Total reads per sample (flag the short ones)" });
</script>
```

## Live result

Drag a selection box across the bad cluster in the mapping-vs-duplication panel — the other panels
restrict to the same samples so you can read their contamination, library and depth.

```{=html}
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
<script src="qc-data.js"></script>
<canvas id="qcHeatLive" width="820" height="420"></canvas>
<canvas id="qcMapLive" width="640" height="360"></canvas>
<canvas id="qcContamLive" width="640" height="360"></canvas>
<canvas id="qcQ30Live" width="640" height="360"></canvas>
<canvas id="qcReadsLive" width="820" height="300"></canvas>
<script>
(function () {
  function draw() {
    if (typeof CanvasXpress === "undefined" || typeof QC_DATA === "undefined") { return setTimeout(draw, 60); }
    var metrics = QC_DATA.y.smps, samples = QC_DATA.y.vars, rows = QC_DATA.y.data;
    var hmData = metrics.map(function (_, c) {
      var col = rows.map(function (r) { return r[c]; });
      var mean = col.reduce(function (a, b) { return a + b; }, 0) / col.length;
      var sd = Math.sqrt(col.reduce(function (a, b) { return a + (b - mean) * (b - mean); }, 0) / col.length) || 1;
      return col.map(function (v) { return Math.round((v - mean) / sd * 100) / 100; });
    });
    new CanvasXpress("qcHeatLive",
      { y: { vars: metrics, smps: samples, data: hmData },
        x: { Batch: QC_DATA.z.Batch, Library: QC_DATA.z.Library } },
      { graphType: "Heatmap", samplesClustered: true, variablesClustered: true,
        colorSpectrum: ["navy", "white", "firebrick3"],
        title: "QC metrics (z-scored) — 96 samples clustered" });
    function panel(id, cfg) {
      new CanvasXpress(id, QC_DATA, Object.assign({ broadcast: true, broadcastGroup: "qc" }, cfg));
    }
    panel("qcMapLive", { graphType: "Scatter2D", xAxis: ["pct_duplication"], yAxis: ["pct_mapped"],
      colorBy: "Batch", sizeBy: "total_reads", title: "Mapping rate vs duplication — select bottom-right" });
    panel("qcContamLive", { graphType: "Scatter2D", xAxis: ["pct_mapped"], yAxis: ["contamination_freemix"],
      colorBy: "Batch", title: "Contamination (freemix) vs mapping rate" });
    panel("qcQ30Live", { graphType: "Scatter2D", xAxis: ["gc_content"], yAxis: ["pct_q30"],
      colorBy: "Library", title: "Q30 vs GC content, coloured by library" });
    panel("qcReadsLive", { graphType: "Bar", graphOrientation: "vertical", xAxis: ["total_reads"],
      colorBy: "Batch", title: "Total reads per sample (flag the short ones)" });
  }
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

The cross-filter is one shared `broadcastGroup` — no framework, no event wiring. Each panel stays a
portable `data` + `config` spec.

## Why "reproducible"

The same specs reproduce the dashboard from R, Python, or a web page, against the same QC table.
